data.name: Ailina
data.gender_notes: Ailina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'ailē' meaning 'rock', and the suffix '-ina' meaning 'little' or 'radiant'. In Greek mythology, Ailina may refer to the goddess Aphrodite, who was born from the foam of the sea. The name evokes images of strength, resilience, and beauty. The name Ailina carries the meaning “Little rock, radiant one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ailina usually hope their child will grow to embody little rock, radiant one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the strength and stability of faith.
data.etymology: Ailina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little rock, radiant one.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ailina total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ailina" has cultural influences rooted in Greek mythology, where 'ailē' is associated with enduring strength. The name was also adopted in the Middle Ages as a devotional name for the Virgin Mary, offering added symbolism and reverence to the chinam.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name "Ailina" holds deep spiritual significance as it reminds us of the rock of our salvation - Jesus Christ. The suffix '-ina' can be seen as a representation of the divine, radiating the love, grace, and healing power of Christ. Additionally, the name highlights the idea that we, as believers, are also called to be strong and resilient in our faith, like a rock in the storm.

historical_references.context: Ailina was a Visigothic princess who is mentioned in historical records as having been married to King Euric of the Visigoths. She is known for her role in the consolidation of the Visigothic kingdom in the Iberian Peninsula.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Ailina remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life.
